The old_supported flag asks only whether the OLD TEXT actually asserts the old statement, not whether it remains current or was objectively correct; a later move or correction does not make this flag false. new_supported likewise asks whether the NEW TEXT contains the new statement, including its uncertainty or plan, not whether it is independently true. CHANGE means the user clearly describes a change between old and new state; CORRECTION means the user explicitly corrects a prior statement. If the pair differs but the text does not establish a change, use CONFLICT or UNCERTAIN. Two careers, hobbies or relationships can coexist; never assume single-valued. A simple "I live in Beijing" then "I live in Shanghai" alone does not establish correction. If a quotation or identity cannot be established, explain uncertainty.
